churches.denomination_detail: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — Presbytery of Michigan and Ontario

score_notes.christology: OPC subscribes to the Westminster Standards — orthodox Trinitarian Christology, Chalcedonian two-natures, virgin birth, bodily resurrection.
score_notes.scripture: Westminster Confession ch. 1 affirms plenary verbal inspiration and inerrancy of the Scriptures as the only rule of faith and life.
score_notes.gender: OPC Book of Church Order restricts the offices of teaching elder, ruling elder, and deacon to qualified men only (1 Tim 2–3; Titus 1).
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of ordained male elders (session) under presbyterian polity with accountability to the presbytery and General Assembly.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology per Westminster — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, effectual calling, perseverance of the saints.
score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: Covenant Orthodox Presbyterian Church is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.

churches.assessment: Fellowship EPC in South Lyon, Michigan began in 1979 as a church plant and joined the Evangelical Presbyterian Church denomination in 1981 — making it effectively a founding-era EPC congregation. Senior Pastor Alan Conrow, who took the role in 2018, holds an impressive theological pedigree: B.A. from Biola University plus M.A.s from both Talbot School of Theology (philosophy of religion) and Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (theology). That dual-seminary background suggests rigorous, thoughtful preaching. Kids Ministry Director Jackie Bullard joined in May 2025. Standard EPC caveat on women-elder policy applies. A solid green-eligible confessional Reformed option in the Detroit metro.

churches.assessment: Free Reformed Grand Rapids is a Dutch Reformed immigrant heritage congregation in West Michigan's dense Reformed corridor — the FRCNA emerged from mid-20th-century Dutch Reformed immigration into Canada and the upper Midwest. Holds the Three Forms of Unity strictly, practices experiential Dutch Reformed preaching (the nadere reformatie tradition), and observes the regulative principle with Psalm-heavy worship. Male-only ordination, traditional sexual ethics. Pastor C. Pronk (emeritus) was a longstanding FRCNA voice; verify current pastoral status. A meaningful option for those drawn to the experiential Dutch Reformed tradition.

churches.assessment: Grace Episcopal Church is the historic home parish of President Gerald R. Ford and Betty Ford, who were married in the old sanctuary in 1948 and whose private funeral was held here in 2006. The parish remains beautiful and historic, with strong choral and liturgical traditions in the Episcopal style. However, for the MOOP rubric, Grace is firmly within The Episcopal Church (TEC) — a denomination that since 1976 has ordained women to all orders, since 2003 has consecrated openly gay bishops, and since 2015 has authorized same-sex marriage rites. These denominational positions place Grace at red on cultural, gender, and denominational dimensions of the rubric. The parish is in a season of transition following the 2024 dissolution-by-merger of the Episcopal Diocese of Western Michigan into the new Diocese of the Great Lakes. Beautiful history. Significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.

churches.denomination_detail: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — Presbytery of Michigan and Ontario

score_notes.christology: OPC subscribes to the Westminster Standards — orthodox Trinitarian Christology, Chalcedonian two-natures, virgin birth, bodily resurrection.
score_notes.scripture: Westminster Confession ch. 1 affirms plenary verbal inspiration and inerrancy of the Scriptures as the only rule of faith and life.
score_notes.gender: OPC Book of Church Order restricts the offices of teaching elder, ruling elder, and deacon to qualified men only (1 Tim 2–3; Titus 1).
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of ordained male elders (session) under presbyterian polity with accountability to the presbytery and General Assembly.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology per Westminster — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, effectual calling, perseverance of the saints.
score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: Harvest Orthodox Presbyterian Church is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.
